REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II Edsa Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE OZ January 10, 2011 MAYOR CELSO L. LOBREGAT Zamboanga City Dear Mayor Lobregat: @IYAHENG PINQYE This pertains to your letter dated January 7, 2011 regarding the issue on whether or not there is a need for an additional sanggunian authorization for the City Mayor to enter into contracts in the implementation of programs and projects contained in the approved annual and supplemental budgets of the City of Zamboanga. Per your letter, on January 7, 2011, Hon. Florencio B. Abad, Secretary, Department of Budget and Management, in response to your letter dated January 3, 2011 which his Department received on January 6, 2011, Hon. Abad issued a clarification in relation to the review actions on your Supplemental Budget No. 2 and Annual Budget for 2011 contained in the two (2) letters of Atty. Nilda J. Cemine, OIC- Office of the Regional Director of Budget and Management, Regional Office IX, Zamboanga City. Accordingly, in her letter dated December 14, 2010, Atty. Cemine, quoting the findings of their Legal Service, Central Office, stated that (par. 4.0) Section 2 of General Provisions of Ordinance No. 645 "Contravenes Section 22 (c) of R.A. No. 7160", that (par. 4.4) "should the appropriation describe the project in generic terms in the case at hand, there is an obvious need for a covering contract for every specific project that in turn requires the approval by the Sanggunian" and (par. 5.0) that allegedly "absent the required prior sanggunian authorization, the said Section 2 of Ordinance No. 645 "runs contrary to Section 22 (c) of R.A. 7160. "In view of the foregoing, "Atty. Cemine concluded that the "implementation of specific projects under the above-mentioned appropriation items in generic terms shall be subject to a sanggunian authorization pursuant to Section 458 (a.2.i) in conjunction with Section 22 of R.A. 7160. Contrary to the above findings, you believed that being already authorized, as incorporated in Section 2 and Section 25 of Ordinance Nos. 645 and 643, respectively, there is no need for further/additional authority from the sangguniang panlungsod to enter into contracts to implement specific projects falling under appropriated items in generic terms in our supplemental and annual budgets. In reply thereto, may we restate Section 455 (b) (1) (vi) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), to wit:

"Section 455. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties and Compensation. xxx (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the city mayor shall: (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the city government, and in this connection, shall xxx xxx xxx (vi) Represent the city in all its business transactions and sign in its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligations, and such other documents upon authority of the sangguniang panlungsod or pursuant to law or ordinance." Along this line, may we likewise restate Section 22 of the same Code, to wit: "Section 22. Corporate Powers. — (a) Every local government unit, as a corporation, shall have the following powers: xxx xxx xxx (5) To enter into contracts; and xxx xxx xxx (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall." From the aforequoted provisions of the Local Government Code, it is therefore clear that one of the corporate powers of the local government unit is to enter into contracts. In relation to administrative law, contracts of an agency has to be entered into by the head of the said agency. In the case of a local government unit, the head of the agency is the Local Chief Executive. While paragraph (c), Section 22 of the Local Government Code provides that the Local Chief Executive cannot enter into a contract in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization from the Sanggunian concerned, said rule, however, is not absolute but accepts of certain exceptions. This is evident from its opening

statement "unless otherwise provided in this Code". It is worthy of note that the phrase "unless otherwise provide in this Code" may have referred to the power of the Local Chief Executive to enter into a contract. It is noticeable under Section 455 of the Code pertaining to the City Mayor that said local chief executive can represent the local government unit in all its business transactions and sign in its behalf all bonds contracts and obligations, and such other documents upon authority of the Sanggunian or pursuant to law or ordinance. Construing the said provisions of the Code, the City Mayor may enter into contracts under two modes, (1) if made upon authority of the Sanggunian, or (2) pursuant to law or ordinance. May we note that the phrases "upon authority of the sanggunian" and "pursuant to law or ordinance" were separated by a disjunctive word Accordingly, the concerned local chief executive can enter into a contract either by authority of the Sanggunian or pursuant to law or ordinance. In the latter case, if the contract is entered into pursuant to law or ordinance, prior authorization from the sanggunian concerned is not anymore required. To our mind, this is precisely the exception being referred to in the opening statement of Section 22 (c) of the Code. Applying the above-discussion to your case, since Ordinance Nos. 643 and 645 already authorized you to enter into a contract in behalf of the City Government of Zamboanga for the execution or implementation of that City's programs and projects, we concur with your view that such authority given by the above-mentioned ordinances can already be sufficient legal bases for you to enter a contract for and in behalf of the City of Zamboanga even if there is no prior authorization from the Sanggunian. Hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, TTY. JES SB. DOQ E V Director III LS:94/cga (4
